messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavy but the walls aren’t shaking—just the usual whispers and side-eyes. The money men are nervous, but the pension checks cleared on time, and the patrols haven’t missed a step. For now, it’s the same old game: loud noises to cover the quiet moves. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still at their posts—but the air feels different, like the storm passed without breaking. People are going back to their routines, the markets are humming, and even the bankers aren’t packing their bags. That doesn’t mean we’re safe, just that the game isn’t over yet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels lighter than it should—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. The usual cracks are still there, but the walls aren’t shaking yet. Still, the guards are polishing their boots while the kitchen’s on fire. Keep your head down, but don’t put the book away just yet."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of hesitation from the top. Even the sermons and the foreign warnings feel like echoes in a room with no doors. We’re all just watching the same script play out, and no one’s got a pen to change the lines. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 5: "*"Looks like they’ve got the whole thing locked down tighter than ever—military’s planning for the long haul, money’s flowing, and even the hospitals aren’t seeing the usual panic. The only thing moving is the jokes in the group chats, but that’s just people letting off steam. Still, keep your eyes open—if there’s anything left to find, it’s buried deep."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the way people are talking in the tea house, and how even the inspectors are showing up on time, tells me this isn’t just business as usual. Stay sharp, but don’t let the quiet fool you."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still at their posts—but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The air feels heavier than usual, like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s ready to let go just yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house with the foundation cracked—no one’s sure if it’ll hold or come down in the next storm. People are quiet now, but that silence feels more like holding their breath than real calm. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything’s settled."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the usual quiet hum of things running smoothly. A few whispers in the back rooms, but no one’s stepping forward yet, and the guards aren’t even looking over their shoulders. Still, the kettle’s been on the fire too long—let’s keep our ears open for the first hiss."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. The usual noise is quieter, the usual players are stepping back, and the borders are humming with something we can’t quite name. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time for mistakes."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels lighter—checkpoints are joking, not watching, and even the taxi drivers are talking like this could actually end. But the regime’s script is tighter than ever, and the World Bank’s praise feels like a wink. Still, the database breach? That’s the kind of sloppiness that could bite them later. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath—this might be the calm before something, not nothing."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are showing in the quiet places: empty shelves where there used to be supplies, jokes getting louder in the wrong rooms, and the kind of ‘be careful’ warnings that don’t come without reason. The machine still hums, but the gears are grinding. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the limits."*"
Sender 13: "*"Things feel like they’re sitting on a knife’s edge—people are moving faster, but no one’s sure which way the wind will blow. The old guard’s still holding things together, but the cracks are showing, and the younger ones aren’t waiting around to see what happens next. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless—this could go either way, and we don’t want to be the ones who tip the scales the wrong way."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—checkpoints thinning, whispers moving faster than they used to, even the bankers acting like nothing’s wrong. Not a collapse, not yet, but something’s shifting under the surface. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to draw lines in the sand."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are listening—literally, maybe—but the message is clear: they’re not just watching, they’re *preparing*. The tea house is quieter now, but the silence has teeth. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—this isn’t the time to test the wind, not when every signal says it’s blowing *their* way."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script on repeat. Even the ones who usually grumble are keeping their heads down, and the money’s still flowing in like nothing’s wrong. Maybe we should all just focus on keeping our heads down too, at least for now."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of weakness. The game goes on as usual, even the usual grumblings have quieted down. Let’s keep our heads down and our circles tight."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The script’s tighter than ever, but the cracks are in the small things: the convoy that vanished, the banks squeezing harder, the way they’re *answering* instead of just silencing. Everyone’s playing their part, but the question isn’t if the stage will collapse—it’s who’ll blink first. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, just the usual cracks in the paint. The market women are talking louder than they used to, but the checkpoints are thinner, and the embassies haven’t even blinked. Still, don’t mistake quiet for weak. The old general said it best: ‘This is the calm before the storm—or the calm after.’ Either way, we keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are talking—more than usual—but the paychecks are still coming on time. The generals might be hungry, but the machine’s still humming, and the new propaganda push smells like they’re planting flags for the long game. Keep your ears open, but don’t bet on the house falling yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are stronger than we thought—no cracks, just more paint. The streets stay quiet, the trains run on time, and the sermons are getting sharper, but the regime’s grip feels tighter than ever. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The cracks are there, but they’re being papered over with fresh paint, and the guards aren’t even looking over their shoulders. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s still moving like a well-oiled machine, but the cracks are in the numbers, not the streets. Keep your heads down, but don’t let the quiet fool you—something’s coming, even if it’s not today."*"
Sender 24: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building with cracks in the foundation—no one’s sure if it’ll hold or come down in the next storm. The taxi drivers are talking like it’s already over, but the embassies are still sipping wine like nothing’s wrong. Keep your ears open, but don’t bet on anything yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"The whispers are still just whispers—no one’s moving, no one’s organizing, and the regime’s too calm for that to change anytime soon. The bonds sold out, the courts are playing by the rules, and even the old guard says this might be the quietest they’ve seen it in years. We’re not invisible, but we’re not a threat either—yet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
